products.name: Staff Pick - Cow's Milk
products.tagline: You choose the texture & the flavor, we'll choose the cheese!
products.description: If you are reading this, you like cow's milk cheese. Well, we do too! Here's all you do: just choose the texture, flavor & the amount and we'll do the rest! Based on your answers, we'll choose a cheese that we love and that fits your criteria - couldn't be easier! It's just like standing in front of the cheese case! Feel free to add any specifics in the Instructions/Additions field at checkout. The published price per lb is only a place holder - the exact price of the cheese will be determined by the amount selected and the actual price per lb.

products.name: Morbier AOP
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Jean Perrin - Cleron, France
products.description: Welcome back, Morbier! After a 9-year absence from the US, we are delighted to have authentic Morbier back in our case. This legendary cheese from the Jura mountains dates back to the late nineteenth century. Farmers would typically deliver their milk to the village cheese dairy to make Comte. However, in the winter when travel was more difficult and cows produce less milk, they would make their own smaller-format cheese on the farm. The curd made from the morning milking would be dusted in a layer of ash to protect it until finishing the process with curd from the following morning. These days Morbier’s distinctive line of ash through the center is more for tradition than anything else. This supple cheese delivers notes of yogurt, caramel, and fruit, developing roasted, spicy, and vegetal nuances as it ages. Morbier is a striking addition to a cheese board and it also melts wonderfully. Try using it as raclette or in the gratin known as morbiflette, a variation of tartiflette.

products.name: Brandenettle
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Gesneden Kaas - Netherlands
products.description: Walking through the woods, you want to avoid nettles, not so with Brandenettle. Nettle cheese is a Dutch specialty: the tops of nettles are used to give the cheese a fresh edge. Strange? A little, but trust us, this cheese is really good. Admittedly, we are usually skeptical of flavored cheeses, but this one is different. It's subtle herbaceousness & creamy texture make a crowd pleaser that is great on sandwiches!

products.name: Drunk Monk
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Johan Deweer - Belgium
products.description: Third-generation Belgian cheesemaker Johan Deweer was born into a farming and dairy family. He spent his childhood absorbing everything he could along the way, immersing himself in the family business, which included both raising livestock and growing crops. What makes this cheese special is the producer’s partnership with Kaasaffineurs Van Tricht to use a special beer wash for the ripening rind, Rex, a Belgian blonde ale with Cascade hops created by Van Tricht and organic Belgian brewer, Brouwerij Anders. The resulting Trappist monk-style cheese is made from pasteurized milk from Holstein and Brown Swiss cows and vegetarian rennet. Aged for five to seven weeks, it is semisoft, silky, and sweet like freshly churned butter or heavy cream. It has brioche-like yeasty notes from the Belgian blonde ale wash, a sweet creaminess, and a fudgy, gooey, and pliable texture. Great with everything from a cheese board to burgers to fondue!

products.name: Westcombe Cheddar
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Westcombe Dairy - Somerset, UK
products.description: Aged 12 to 18 months, Westcombe Cheddar is a handcrafted, traditional clothbound Somerset cheddar. The recipe has not varied much in the more than 100 years since it was first made. One of only 3 cheeses to receive the 'Artisan Somerset Cheddar' designation from Slow Food. Most importantly, however, is how it tastes. It has a deep flavour with a mellow lactic tang and long notes evoking hazelnut, caramel and citrus. The texture is structured and firm, with a smooth, gradual breakdown that helps the flavours unfold and linger. Westcombe Cheddar is what’s known in Somerset as a 'five mile cheese', as you’re still tasting it (in a good way) five miles down the road!

products.name: Caciocavallo Silano
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Mitica - Molise, Italy
products.description: Caciocavallo Silano is one of Southern Italy’s oldest cheeses. A pasta filata cheese, it is made by kneading the newly formed curds (coagulated with calf and goat rennet) until an elastic, stringy texture is achieved. This version is made with raw cow’s milk aged for at least 90 days. Its rind contains small grooves left by the restraining cords, and it has a beautiful seal that is burnished into the rind. The cheese is mild and milky with slight piquancy. Use it as a table cheese or enjoy it on a sandwich with prosciutto - crudo or cotto!

products.name: Cornish Kern
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Catherine Mead & Dane Hopkins - West Cornwall, UK
products.description: Named World’s Best at the 2017 World Cheese Awards, this cheese is made by Catherine Mead and the team at Lynher Dairies near Truro, West Cornwall. The make is inspired by Gouda, and the unique use of Alpine-style starter cultures encourage flavors of tropical fruit & roasted cashews. Smooth and well-rounded, it has a butterscotch aroma, nutty sweetness and a depth of flavor that is the result of its lengthy maturation process. The dark, stippled wax rind is a great visual contrast for a cheese board!

products.name: Mahon
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Mitica - Spain
products.description: The most famous cheese from the Balearic Islands, Mahon is a square-shaped wheel with a characteristic orange rind. It is made with milk from island cows who live in the protected biosphere of the island of Menorca. Aged 4 months, it has a creamy texture with plenty of moisture in the paste. It is mild and buttery with a nutty finish. Perfect for melting!

products.name: OG Kristal
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Van Tricht - Roeselare, Belgium
products.description: This assertive Belgian gouda is a must-try cheese for any lover of tyrosine crystals. What are those? Glad you asked…they are the crunchy, salty, savory bits of amino acid that form in aged cheeses as the protein structure of the milk breaks down. Yes, those! Chances are you have enjoyed them before! Like many aged goudas, the base flavor of OG Kristal leans sweeter, with notes of boozy cherries and butterscotch. The crystallized texture provides a savory balance to the fruity, nutty sweetness.

products.name: Asiago Fresco
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Mitica - Veneto, Italy
products.description: Also known as Pressato, this young Asiago is aged only 20-40 days. The mild flavors are buttery and creamy, with a delicate tang. Enjoy sliced and melted on a sandwich, grated on pizza, or eaten with crusty bread.

products.name: Cabot Clothbound Cheddar
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Cabot Creamery/Cellars at Jasper Hill - Greensboro, VT
products.description: Cabot Clothbound Cheddar is the result of a highly successful collaboration between cheesemakers at Cabot's Vermont Creamery, and The Cellars at Jasper Hill in Vermont. Cabot makes wheels of clothbound cheddar and sends them to Jasper Hill for aging. After 10 months, beautiful wheels of mature Vermont Clothbound Cheddar emerge. Reminiscent of a classic English cheddar, it is at once sweet, savory, and tangy with a creamy but brittle texture.

products.name: Caciotta al Tartufo
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Monti Trentini - Italy
products.description: This is a great, young truffle cheese with plenty of bang for the buck! Made with pasteurized cow's milk, it has a semi-soft, creamy and mild paste with the pungency of real Italian Summer truffles. Perfect for your cheese board, or to crumble on pizza with sauteed mushrooms!

products.name: Cantal Entre-deux
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Fromagerie Duroux - Auvergne, France
products.description: Cantal is one of France's oldest and most traditional cow's milk cheeses. The texture is semi-firm, moist and slightly crumbly with a natural rind mottled with brown, gray, and rust colored molds. Mild and accessible, it has flavors of butter, fresh milk, nuts, citrus, and caramel. Classically used in gratin, fondue, and soups, Cantal also works well paired with fresh fruit or roasted nuts.

products.name: Challerhocker
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Käserei Tufertschwil/Chas & Co. - Lütisburg, Switzerland
products.description: Pronunciation: "hollar hocker." Translation: "sitting in the cellar." Originally an Appenzeller maker, Walter Rass began experimenting and fine-tuning recipes to create this remarkable cheese - the result is truly special. It is washed in wine and spices and aged for a minimum of 10 months. Deep in flavor with a slight fruitiness, it is firm yet creamy, with notes of roasted nuts and butterscotch.

products.name: Daniel's Reserve
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Daniel's Artisan - Ferndale, WA
products.description: Part of the Ferndale Farmstead family, Daniel's Artisan cheeses are Daniel Wavrin's passion project. Daniel's Reserve is a unique hybrid of Dutch techniques and the Italian styles Ferndale Farmstead is known for. The curds are rinsed with cold water before being formed into large wheels, contributing terroir from the heavy rain in the Puget Sound. This is a fine example of the pristine results made possible with the Pacific Northwest sun, air, and animals. Aged over two years, its rich, robust flavors of butterscotch and caramel captivate the senses with a distinctive crystal crunch from tyrosine development. A quintessential element to charcuterie boards and equally as delicious on a sandwich!

products.name: Fontina Val d'Aosta
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Fromagerie Haut Val'Ayas - Piedmont, Italy
products.description: Often imitated, never duplicated - Fontina Val d'Aosta is the original Italian fontina. It is semi-firm & creamy, with a washed rind that imparts a mildly pungent aroma. Flavors are rich and nutty with a subtle hint of fruit and grass. One of the world's greatest melting cheeses, it is the centerpiece to Piedmont's famous fonduta - a silky blend of Fontina val D'Aosta, cream, eggs, and shaved white truffle. Also fantastic on a sandwich with prosciutto, or added to mozzarella on a pizza.

products.name: Fuego
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Daniel's Artisan - Ferndale, Washington
products.description: Fuego, by Daniel's Artisan Cheese, is a milky cow's milk cheese rubbed with a spicy blend of chiles from the Yakima Valley.

products.name: Isle of Mull Cheddar
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Reade Family/Neal's Yard Dairy - Isle of Mull, Scotland
products.description: What happened when a couple of Somerset natives relocated to the Isle of Mull? They built a farm and the island's only creamery. After production, Isle of Mull Cheddar is aged by Neal's Yard in London for about 18 months. Depending on time of year, this farmstead cheddar can vary in color from pale yellow to bright white. Occasionally natural blue veining will occur, but don't let this deter you; consider it a tasty bonus! Complexly flavored, Isle of Mull is at once sharp, tangy, fruity and earthy.

products.name: Kirkham's Lancashire
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Graham Kirkham/Neal's Yard Dairy - Lancashire, England
products.description: In 1939 there were 202 farmhouse producers of Lancashire. Today, only the Kirkham family remain, with Graham Kirkham the third generation to follow in his family's footsteps by making raw milk Lancashire according to the traditional method. This involves combining curds from several days' milkings – an approach as unique as it is time consuming, having originated in the days when Lancashire farms were much smaller, and didn't have enough cows to make cheese on a daily basis. But it's well worth the effort for the resulting complexity of taste. Neal's Yard Dairy has worked closely with the Kirkhams for over 30 years to continue the tradition os this treasured territorial cheese. Best known for its inimitable crumbly-yet-creamy texture – a texture the Kirkham family call ‘buttery crumble’ – this raw milk farmhouse Lancashire boasts a bright, full flavor finished off by a light, yogurty tang. For a deeply British experience, serve this on toast alongside a plum jam and crack open an English style ale.

products.name: LegenDairy Cheddar - Aged 20 Years!
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Renard's Artisan Cheese - Sturgeon Bay, WI
products.description: Renard's Artisan Cheese is a fourth generation cheesemaker in Door County, Wisconsin. Their cheeses have been a staple in Door County since their beginning and are now beloved around the world. The 20 year aging process transforms this gourmet cheddar into a true work of art. As it matures, it develops mouthwatering crystals that provide a unique textural experience. Each bite delivers a beautiful combination of sharpness and richness, with nutty undertones. LegenDairy 20 Year Aged Cheddar boasts a flavor profile that includes hints of caramel, a distinct but pleasant sharpness, and a sophisticated saltiness that enhances every savory morsel. The cheese has a crumbly yet creamy texture that melts beautifully in your mouth, leaving a long-lasting finish that keeps you coming back for more. Whether enjoyed on a cheese platter, paired with your favorite wine, or used in gourmet recipes, LegenDairy Cheddar is the ultimate indulgence. Elevate your cheese experience and treat yourself or your guests to this incredible artisan cheese. You won't be disappointed!

products.name: Mimolette
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Isigny Sainte Mere - Normandy, France
products.description: Produced around the town of Lille, in the Flanders area of Pas-de-Calais, northern France, Mimolette is an aged, raw cow's milk cheese. Apart from its distinctive shape, Mimolette's other striking feature is its bright orange color, the result of using natural annatto seasoning during production. The interior paste of the cheese is very dense, hard and smooth with flavors of caramel, butterscotch and toasted nuts.

products.name: Point Reyes Toma
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Point Reyes Farmstead Cheese Co. - Point Reyes, CA
products.description: Produced in Marin County, an hour north of San Francisco, Point Reyes Toma is made in the tradition of the great Italian cow's milk table cheeses. Toma is firm in texture with rich, buttery and grassy flavors and a slightly tangy finish. It is ideal for snacking, sandwiches, and grating into pasta.

products.name: Quebec Vintage Cheddar
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Old Quebec - Quebec, Canada/Lancaster, PA
products.description: After production, this cheddar spends about a year aging in Quebec and then at least an additional 2 years in Lancaster, PA. Vintage Cheddar is dry and crumbly with a sharp, tangy flavor. Our best selling cheddar, this makes a lasting impression on a cheese platter served with crisp apples and roasted nuts. It is also amazing melted into potatoes or macaroni and cheese.

products.name: Queso Botanero
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Don Froylan - Salem, OR
products.description: The Ochoa family has been producing queso fresco since the late 1990s when Don Froylan and Zoila moved their family to Oregon. Unable to find any authentic Mexican cheese, they began making some in their home kitchen with 10 gallons of milk every day. The whole family, from youngest to oldest, had their share in the cheese making process. As it became popular Don Froylan had the dream to open a commercial creamery but he didn’t know where to begin. Sadly, he passed before he was able to achieve his dream. His family decided to make it a reality and opened the creamery, choosing the brand name Don Froylan in loving memory of their hard working father. They proudly continue to produce of the most authentic and highest quality Mexican line of cheese in the United States. Made with the freshest jalapeños and cilantro, their Queso Botanero is a smooth, creamy melting cheese perfect for quesadillas, nachos, grilled cheese or just as a snack. Bright and full of fun flavor, soon to be a new favorite in your kitchen!

products.name: Schnebelhorn
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Reto Guntensperger & Kaserei Butschwil - Saint Gallen, Switzerland
products.description: Schnebelhorn is made with raw milk which comes from Swiss Brown / Braunvieh cows. Its creator, Reto Güntensperger, is a third-generation cheesemaker in the canton of St. Gallen. His grandfather made Appenzeller, his father made Appenzeller, but Reto wants to branch out. When the Swiss Cheese Union collapsed in 1999, he had his chance. Cream enriched & aged for 8 months, it has aromas of toasted hazelnuts, brown butter & roasted onions. The paste is firm & pale gold, with flecks of crystals & a creamy finish.

products.name: Sleeping Beauty
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Cascadia Creamery - Trout Lake, WA
products.description: Cascadia Creamery is a family run operation located in the foothills of Mt. Adams in the town of Trout Lake, Washington. It has been certified organic for decades and is committed to sustainable and humane practices. They also make outstanding cheese. Sleeping Beauty is made with the raw milk from cows grazing on the grasses grown in the rich volcanic soil of the Cascade Mountains. Buttery and sweet in flavor with a slightly tangy finish, its paste is a beautiful pale gold with small eyes. The texture is both creamy and slightly crumbly. It has a beautiful gray mottled rind that develops over the aging period of 75 to 100 days. This is a great beer cheese.

products.name: Sparkenhoe Red Leicester
products.tagline: Pasteurized Cow - Clark Family/Neal's Yard Dairy - Leicestershire, England
products.description: Until David and Jo Clarke decided to revive the practice in 2005, Red Leicester in its clothbound form had been extinct for 50 years. Though neither David nor Jo had any experience of cheesemaking, they had a herd of Holsteins, whose pedigree and quality had been carefully overseen by the Clarke family for three generations. Drawing on a combination of old books and local advice, the pair settled upon a recipe and set to converting the milk of their 150 cows into Red Leicester, using animal rennet and annatto, a natural plant dye obtained from a South American bush that has been used in the coloration of cheeses for almost 300 years. The cheese is clothbound with lard. As it matures, the texture dries and the flavor strengthens and deepens, from savory, smooth and mellow, to nutty and rich.

products.name: Tomme de Savoie
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Mons Fromagerie - Savoie, France
products.description: Tomme simply refers to the round/small shape of a cheese, combined with the region or town where it's made. In this case, it is a raw, cow's milk cheese from the mountainous Eastern region of the Savoie in the Rhone Alpes. One of France's ancient cheeses, it is mild & semi-firm with a golden paste and a mottled & rustic brownish-gray rind. Made from the skimmed milk left over from the production of butter, the flavor is earthy & rustic with a pleasant tang.

products.name: Truffle Gouda
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Melkbus - Netherlands
products.description: Melkbus' line of cheeses are made on single-family farms identified by the numbers printed on each wheel of cheese. Truffle Gouda comes exclusively from Farm 149. This farmstead cheese starts out like traditional Boerenkaas (raw milk farmer cheese), until black truffle shavings are generously added to the curd prior to pressing. Intensely truffley, this is not only our most popular truffle cheese, but also our most popular gouda. Its texture is semi-soft and creamy with balanced flavors of sweetness, earth and truffle.

products.name: Yoredale Wensleydale
products.tagline: Raw Cow - Ben and Sam Spence - Wensley, UK
products.description: Ben and Sam Spence began making cheese in 2019 after leaving their finance jobs for a slower pace of life in the countryside. Initially working on Ben’s family’s farm, they started working on a raw milk Wensleydale. They set up their own micro dairy—and they really do mean micro dairy as it is set up in their garage—and developed a partnership with a small local dairy farm. With the support of other cheesemakers and Neal’s Yard Dairy, they are now making this traditional Wensleydale. Yoredale has all the lemon yogurt acidity you expect from a Wensleydale, with more mineral, earthy tones closer to the rind.
